title: Stock operations overview
summary: Understand the stock dashboard, lifecycle statuses, filters and the demand-versus-supply view for every physical Denago unit.

body.text: Stock operations tracks every physical Denago unit from supplier order through reservation, PDI, delivery and warranty activation. Anyone with stock access can view the inventory; creating orders and moving units requires the **stock.manage** permission.
Reading the dashboard

The metric cards at the top summarise your inventory: **Available** (with total landed value), **Incoming & inspection**, **Committed** (reserved plus allocated) and **Average stock age**. A warning banner appears when items need attention.

items: Reservations expiring within 24 hours
Overdue purchase orders (past their expected date)
Received units still missing a serial
Available units held for more than 60 days

body.text: The stock lifecycle
Each unit sits in exactly one lifecycle status. Units move through the chain below; the list view sorts exceptions (hold, damaged, ready) to the top so they are never missed.

rows: On order from a supplier, not yet arrived
Received, pending physical check and serial capture
In stock and ready to reserve or allocate
PDI passed, ready for customer handover
Handed over; now a customer vehicle
Removed from normal flow pending a decision

body.text: Finding a unit

items: Use the search box to match on serial, stock number, model, colour, PO reference or customer name.
Narrow with the model, location and age (30/60/90+ days) selectors, then choose Filter.
Use the status pills to jump to a single stage, for example Available or Ready.
Open any row to see the unit's full identity, history and next actions.

body.text: Demand versus supply
The demand-versus-supply panel compares open CRM leads against available and incoming stock for each model, flagging shortages so purchasing stays ahead of sales demand.
Landed cost figures and the manager quick-links (ageing stock, receiving queue, ready for revenue) are only shown to users with stock.manage.

title: Purchase orders and receiving stock
summary: Raise supplier purchase orders, receive arrivals partially or in full, and cancel outstanding orders.

body.text: Purchase orders bring new units into the system as **incoming** stock. Receiving moves arrived units into inspection. These actions require the **stock.manage** permission.
Raising a purchase order

items: From Stock operations, choose Purchase order.
Set the supplier (defaults to Denago), an optional reference, expected date and notes.
Add one or more lines, each with a product, optional colour, quantity, unit cost and freight.
Submit. One incoming stock unit is created for every quantity ordered, each carrying the line's cost.

body.text: Quantity per line is capped between 1 and 200. The order opens in the Ordered state and appears under Open purchase orders until fully received or cancelled.
Receiving arrivals
Receiving supports genuine partial receipts. You can receive everything at once, or take in only some units per line and receive the rest later.

items: Under Open purchase orders, choose Receive on the relevant order.
Enter how many units to receive against each line (or receive all outstanding).
Add an optional receipt reference and notes, then confirm.

body.text: Received units move to **Awaiting inspection** and are stamped with an arrival date. The order becomes **Partially received** while units remain outstanding, or **Received** once nothing is left. A goods receipt is recorded for the audit trail.
Received units are not yet sellable. They must pass inspection before becoming Available.
Cancelling an order

items: Choose Cancel on an open (ordered or partially received) purchase order.
Enter a reason and confirm.

body.text: Cancelling removes only the still-incoming units. Units already received remain in stock. Cancellation cannot be undone.

title: Inspecting arrivals and capturing serials
summary: Complete the inspection step that turns a received unit into available stock, capturing its serial, condition and stock number.

body.text: Every received unit passes through inspection before it can be sold. Inspection captures the serial/VIN, confirms condition and assigns the stock number. Requires **stock.manage**.
Inspecting a received unit

items: Open a unit that is Awaiting inspection (filter the list by Inspection, or use the Receiving queue quick-link).
Choose Inspect arrival under Workflow actions.
Enter the serial/VIN (required) and the storage location.
Set the inspection result: Accepted into available stock, or Damaged / quarantine.
Add condition notes and complete the inspection.

body.text: Accepted units become **Available** with condition set to new. Rejected units become **Damaged** for a later repair or disposal decision. A stock number in the form STK-YEAR-0001 is assigned automatically if the unit does not already have one.
Serials are unique across active stock, case-insensitively. If a serial is already assigned to another live unit, the save is blocked. The dashboard also flags received units still missing a serial.
Adding a floor unit directly

For stock that did not come through a purchase order (for example an existing showroom unit), use **Add floor unit** on the Stock operations page. It creates the unit as Available immediately, with its cost recorded as the landed cost.

title: Reserving and allocating units
summary: Hold available stock for a lead, record deposits, release holds, and commit a unit to an accepted quote.

body.text: Available units can be reserved against an open lead or allocated directly to an accepted quote. Both actions require **stock.manage** and access to the linked lead or quote.
Reserving for a lead

items: Open an Available unit and choose Reserve for lead.
Pick an open lead, set the reservation length (1 to 30 days, default 3) and any required deposit.
Reserve the unit.

body.text: The unit moves to **Reserved** and the reservation record becomes the source of truth for its expiry and deposit. The lead's product must match the unit.
Reservations expire automatically once past their expiry time, returning the unit to Available. Reservations expiring within 24 hours are flagged on the dashboard.
Recording a deposit
While a unit is reserved, choose **Record deposit**, enter the payment reference and confirm. The deposit-received time is stored against the reservation.
Releasing a hold

items: Open a Reserved or Allocated unit and choose Release.
Enter a reason and confirm.

body.text: The unit returns to **Available**, the active reservation is marked released and any quote link is cleared.
Allocating to an accepted quote

items: Open an Available or Reserved unit and choose Allocate accepted quote.
Select an accepted quote that contains this product as a selected line.
Allocate to the quote.

body.text: The unit moves to **Allocated** and any active reservation is converted to that quote. Only accepted quotes containing the matching, selected product can be chosen.
If another user reserves or allocates the same unit first, your action is rejected. Refresh and pick another unit.

title: PDI, delivery and warranty activation
summary: Move an allocated unit through pre-delivery inspection, complete the customer handover, and activate warranty.

body.text: Once a unit is allocated to an accepted quote it enters the delivery pipeline: PDI, then handover. Delivery creates the customer's vehicle record and starts the warranty. Requires **stock.manage**.
Running pre-delivery inspection

items: Open an Allocated unit and choose Start PDI. The unit moves to PDI with its checklist in progress.
When work is done, choose Complete PDI.
Set the outcome: Passed (ready for delivery) or Failed (place on hold).
Record any issues or work completed, then confirm.

body.text: A passed PDI moves the unit to **Ready for delivery**. A failed PDI places it on **Hold** with the issues appended to the unit's notes.
Completing the handover

items: Open a Ready-for-delivery unit and choose Complete delivery.
Set the warranty length in months (default 12) and confirm.

body.text: On delivery the unit becomes **Delivered** and the system records the per-unit sale value from the quote line (unit price less its discount), the delivery date and the warranty window. A customer vehicle record is created automatically from the unit's model, serial (VIN), colour and owner, unless a vehicle with that VIN already exists.
A unit can only be delivered if it is PDI-passed and allocated to an accepted quote that is linked to a contact. Deliveries are final; Delivered units have no further transitions.
Holds and damaged units can be sent back into the workflow: resolve a hold to return it to available (or allocated if a quote is attached), or send a damaged unit for assessment.

title: Labels, custom statuses and unit records
summary: Tag units with organisational labels, manage custom statuses, edit unit details including landed cost, and archive units.

body.text: Beyond the fixed lifecycle status, each unit can carry an organisational label, and the unit record holds its full identity, cost basis and history. These actions require **stock.manage**.
Labels versus lifecycle status

A unit is always in exactly one lifecycle status (incoming through delivered). Separately, it may carry one optional **label** such as demo unit, showroom floor, consignment or management hold. Labels are for organising and flagging stock; they never change the workflow.

items: Open a unit and choose Label.
Pick a label from the list, or No label to clear it, and save.

body.text: The label list is fully editable in Settings, Stock. Adding or removing a label needs no data migration. Removing a label clears it from any units that carried it.

The four built-in statuses (On order, Available, Reserved, Sold) are load-bearing and cannot be removed. Additional custom statuses can be defined in settings as organisational labels for the status field.
Editing unit details

Choose **Edit details** on a unit to update its serial/VIN, colour, location, condition, battery and charger serials, odometer, internal notes, and both the acquisition cost and the landed cost. Landed cost is the inventory value used across the dashboard and reporting.
Unit history and archiving
Every unit page shows an append-only lifecycle history of who did what and when, plus its commercial allocation (lead or quote) and warranty once delivered.

items: To retire a unit, open it and choose Remove from active stock.
Enter a reason and confirm. The record is archived but its audit history is retained.

body.text: Units that are reserved, allocated, in PDI, ready, delivered or sold cannot be archived. Release or complete the active workflow first.

title: Managing the product catalogue
summary: Maintain the Denago models, colours, SKUs and base prices that stock, leads, quotes and vehicles all share.

body.text: The product catalogue holds the Denago models your team sells. Stock, leads, quotes and customer vehicles all reference the same product data, so keeping it accurate keeps every module consistent. Creating and editing products requires owner-level access.
Adding a product

items: On the Product catalogue page choose New product.
Enter the model name (required), and optionally an SKU, category and base price.
Add a description and any launch colours (comma-separated), then save.

body.text: Editing a product

items: Open a product from the catalogue list.
Update the name, SKU, category, base price or description in the Details panel and save.
Toggle Active to control whether the model is offered on new leads. Inactive models stay linked to existing records.

body.text: Managing colours
In the Colours panel, add a colour with the field provided, or remove one with the delete control. These colours feed the colour pickers on stock units, purchase orders and vehicle registration.
Each product shows how many leads and vehicles reference it, so you can see usage before making changes.
Deleting a product moves it to the Trash for 60 days rather than removing it outright. Existing leads and vehicles keep their link to it.

title: Managing workshop parts
summary: Create parts with pricing and storage location, track stock levels, set reorder alerts, and adjust quantities.

body.text: Parts is the workshop's consumables inventory. Each part record supports job-card billing, stock control and purchasing decisions. Managing parts requires the **parts.manage** permission.
Adding a part

items: On the Parts page choose New part.
Enter the name (required), and optionally an SKU/code and a storage location (shelf or bin).
Set the sell price and cost, the opening stock quantity, and a reorder level for low-stock alerts.
Add any notes and save.

body.text: Adjusting stock levels

Choose **Manage** on a part to adjust its quantity. Enter a positive number for stock received or a negative number for a correction, then apply. Each adjustment is written to the audit log with the resulting balance.
Low-stock monitoring
When a part's quantity falls to or below its reorder level, it is highlighted in the list and counted in the page header so replenishment happens before parts run out.
From Manage you can also edit a part's details or remove it. Pricing and stock levels remain editable at any time. Parts are available for selection on job cards along with their selling price.

title: Registering customer vehicles
summary: Register a vehicle to its owner with identity, warranty and service data, or let delivery create it automatically.

body.text: The vehicle fleet is every unit owned by your customers. A vehicle can be created automatically when a stock unit is delivered, or registered manually. Viewing vehicles needs a vehicles view permission; registering requires **vehicles.manage**.
Registering a vehicle

items: On the Vehicle fleet page choose Register vehicle.
Select the owner (contact) and product; the model auto-fills from the product if left blank.
Add the VIN/serial, registration number, colour and purchase date.
Set the warranty months and the service intervals in kilometres and months.
Optionally record an initial odometer reading, then register.

body.text: Registration links the vehicle to the owner's permanent sales and service timeline, records the audit entry, and logs the initial reading as the mileage baseline.

For a new delivery, the review request and delivery survey can be triggered automatically after registration. When a stock unit is delivered, its vehicle is created for you from the model, VIN, colour and warranty.
The fleet list
The list shows each vehicle's model, owner, VIN, current kilometres, next service and a status badge. Use the **Service due** toggle to show only vehicles that are overdue or due soon.
Users with owned-only access see just their own customers' vehicles; those with view-all see the whole fleet.

title: Service history and mileage tracking
summary: Log services and odometer readings, and understand how the CRM calculates when a vehicle is next due.

body.text: Each vehicle page tracks its service history and mileage, driving the due-status shown across the fleet. These actions require **vehicles.manage** access to the vehicle.
Recording a service

items: Open a vehicle and use the Service history form.
Enter a summary (required), the date and the mileage.
Optionally set the next-due kilometres and date; leave blank to fall back to the vehicle's intervals.
Add any details and add the service record.

body.text: Recording a service with a mileage value also adds a mileage log entry, keeping the current-kilometre figure accurate. Services created from a job card show the job-card number.
Logging mileage
Use the Mileage log to add an odometer reading at any time with an optional note. The most recent reading is treated as the vehicle's current kilometres.
How next service is calculated
Explicit next-due values on the latest service win. Otherwise the CRM applies the vehicle's service intervals from the last service (or the purchase date for time, and zero for distance).

rows: Past the due date or over the due kilometres
Within 30 days or 200 km of due
Comfortably ahead of the next service
No intervals or due data set

body.text: Deleting a service or mileage entry is recorded in the customer history for accountability.

title: Battery health and warranty claims
summary: Log battery state-of-health checks to track degradation, and manage a vehicle's warranty status and claims.

body.text: For EVs, the vehicle page tracks battery health over time and manages warranty and claims. These actions require **vehicles.manage** access to the vehicle.
Logging a battery check

items: Open a vehicle and use the Battery health form.
Enter the state of health (0 to 100%), voltage, cycle count and pack serial as available.
Add any notes and log the check.

body.text: Checks build a state-of-health trend chart. The CRM highlights the latest reading, estimated monthly degradation, projected months to the 60% threshold, and flags when a check indicates a warranty claim or a battery-replacement opportunity.
Log state of health at every service to build a reliable degradation trend. Readings are colour-coded: 80%+ healthy, 60 to 79% caution, below 60% critical.
Warranty and claims
The Warranty panel shows the current warranty status and expiry, derived from the purchase date and warranty months. To raise a claim, describe the fault and log it.

items: Log a claim with a description of the fault.
Use the status selector on a claim to update its progress and add a resolution note.
Update to save, or remove a claim with the delete control.

body.text: Vehicle documents can be attached in the Documents panel, and a job card can be opened directly from the vehicle for workshop work.
